mission_02: Z-score outlier detection is a parametric method that measures how many standard deviations each data point lies from the mean. Under the assumption of normality, approximately 99.7% of data falls within 3 standard deviations, making points beyond this threshold statistically rare. The standard Z-score uses mean and standard deviation, which are themselves sensitive to outliers. The modified Z-score addresses this by using the median and MAD (Median Absolute Deviation), which are robust statistics resistant to extreme values. The constant 0.6745 scales the MAD to be comparable to the standard deviation for normally distributed data. Z-score methods are ideal when data is approximately normal and you need a simple, interpretable outlier detection approach with clear statistical justification.
